1358.0.0.description:
Log TestSuite PostRun failure for results publishing

Test-harness step (not a functional test): logs the test-suite post-run outcome for results publishing. Excluded from manual-test coverage mapping.

1358.1001.0.description:
Log TestSet setup outcome

Test-harness step (not a functional test): logs the per-test-set setup outcome before the set's functional cases run. Excluded from manual-test coverage mapping.

1358.1001.1.description:
Basic check that all devices are providing POE

[Log-derived analysis] Basic PoE delivery check across the setup's PoE-capable switches. For each PoE device it enables the PoE port feeding a powered device, starts a DHCP server toward that client, and verifies the client comes up and is reachable by ping (confirming power is being supplied). Confirms non-PoE ports report Off/Disabled with zero power, then disables PoE on the port and verifies the client stops responding, re-enables it and verifies power is restored. Restores and verifies the configuration afterwards.

1358.1001.2.description:
Check device reporting of POE status

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies the switch's reporting of PoE status via show power-inline. With a powered device attached, it confirms the device-level fields (nominal power non-zero, actual consumption non-zero, legacy-device detection state) and the per-port fields (powered-device type, configured priority, current power consumption, powered-device class) are reported correctly. Toggles PoE admin off then on and confirms the reported consumption tracks the change (drops to zero when off, rises when restored) while the port still detects the connected device.

1358.1001.3.description:
Check POE is supplied for all priority settings

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies PoE is supplied correctly under every port priority setting. For each priority (critical, high, low) it sets the port priority, confirms the powered device stays powered and reachable, confirms the configured/actual priority is reported correctly, then disables PoE to confirm power stops and re-enables it to confirm the priority setting is retained and power is restored.

1358.1001.4.description:
Check POE Spare-pair of 2-pair POE devices

[Inferred behavior - case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Intended to verify PoE delivery over the spare pair of 2-pair (4-pair-capable) PoE powered devices. Reported UNSUPPORTED because no 2-pair PoE devices are configured on this test setup.

1358.1001.5.description:
Check POE Data-pair of 2-pair POE devices

[Inferred behavior - case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Intended to verify PoE delivery over the data pair of 2-pair (4-pair-capable) PoE powered devices. Reported UNSUPPORTED because no 2-pair PoE devices are configured on this test setup.

1358.1001.6.description:
Check global disable/enable of POE

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies global disable/enable of PoE. With a powered device active, it globally disables PoE and confirms power is withdrawn (client unreachable, power-inline reported as disabled at both device and port level), then globally re-enables PoE and confirms the device is powered again and reporting normally.

1358.1001.7.description:
Check high-availability network power behaviour

[Inferred behavior - case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Intended to verify High-Availability Network Power (HANP) behaviour: that with HANP enabled the switch maintains uninterrupted PoE to powered devices across a DUT reboot, and that without HANP power is interrupted during the reboot. Reported UNSUPPORTED because no HANP-capable PoE devices are configured on this test setup.

1358.1001.8.description:
Check POE four-wire single-signature mode of 2-pair POE devices

[Inferred behavior - case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Intended to verify PoE four-wire single-signature mode on 2-pair (4-pair-capable) PoE powered devices. Reported UNSUPPORTED because no 2-pair PoE devices are configured on this test setup.

1358.1001.9.description:
Check legacy-mode enable is persistent over reboot

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that the PoE legacy-detection mode setting persists across a reboot. Confirms PoE is provided by default, enables legacy mode and confirms power continues with legacy detection reported as enabled, reboots and confirms the enabled state persists. Then disables legacy mode, confirms power continues with legacy detection reported as disabled, reboots again and confirms the disabled state also persists.

1358.1001.10.description:
Check HANP works after PoE is restored after stopping

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies HANP continues to work after the PoE subsystem is forcibly stopped and restored. With HANP enabled, it kills the PoE/PoEHW processes (via simulated fail/kill and healthcheck cycles), waits for the subsystem to recover, and confirms the powered device regains connectivity. It then reboots the DUT and confirms PoE is maintained uninterrupted across the reboot (continuous ping response) and that the HANP negotiation is preserved.

1358.1001.56299.description:
PoE is restored after stopping

[Log-derived analysis] Regression check that PoE is correctly restored after the PoE subsystem is stopped. With a powered device active, it forcibly kills the PoE/PoEHW processes (simulated fail kill and healthcheck cycles), waits for core generation and recovery, and confirms after each cycle that the powered device regains connectivity and the switch reports PoE normally.

1358.1001.65718.description:
Check global disable of POE is persistent over reboot

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that a global PoE disable persists across a reboot. Confirms PoE is provided by default, globally disables PoE and confirms power is withdrawn, saves config and reboots, then confirms PoE remains disabled after the reboot. Re-enables PoE globally and confirms power is provided again.

1358.1001.65952.description:
Check POE is provided to a non-autoclass PD when port is set to autoclass

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies PoE continues to be supplied to a non-autoclass powered device when the feeding port is configured for autoclass. Confirms power by default, sets the port to autoclass and confirms the device stays powered, saves config and reboots to confirm power persists, then disables autoclass and confirms the device remains powered.

1358.1001.657182.description:
Check port-disable of POE is persistent over reboot

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that a per-port PoE disable persists across a reboot. Confirms PoE is provided by default, disables PoE on the port and confirms power stops, saves config and reboots, then confirms PoE remains disabled on that port after the reboot. Re-enables PoE on the port and confirms power is restored.

1358.1001.729481.description:
Check port-disable of POE is persistent over rolling-reboot

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that a per-port PoE disable persists across a stack rolling-reboot. On a multi-member stack feeding powered devices, it confirms power by default, disables PoE on the ports and confirms power stops, performs a rolling-reboot, and confirms the ports remain PoE-disabled afterwards. Re-enables PoE and confirms power is restored, checking stack health and config consistency throughout.

1358.1001.729482.description:
Check POE is persistent over rolling-reboot

[Log-derived analysis] Verifies that PoE delivery persists across a stack rolling-reboot. On a multi-member stack feeding powered devices, it confirms power is provided by default, performs a rolling-reboot, and confirms the powered devices remain powered and reachable afterwards, with the stack returning to a healthy synced state and config unchanged.
